text: Uttar Pradesh is almost exactly the size of the United Kingdom. Slide Britain onto it at true scale, and the two outlines nearly match: about two hundred and forty one thousand square kilometres against two hundred and forty two and a half thousand. The difference is less than one percent. And Uttar Pradesh isn't even India's biggest state.

So here's the challenge. India has twenty eight states, and every single one of them has a country twin, a nation of almost the same size. Some of them match to within a few dozen square kilometres. We'll go from the biggest state to the smallest, slide each country onto India at its true size, and at the end, count the closest matches.

First, the rules. India covers about three point two nine million square kilometres. State areas come from India's Ministry of Statistics, and country areas from Encyclopaedia Britannica, both as total area. Union territories like Delhi, Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir sit this one out. Today it's states only. Every country you see is moved without stretching, so its size on screen is honest.

Number one: Rajasthan, about three hundred and forty two thousand square kilometres, the largest state in India. Its closest twin is the Republic of the Congo in Central Africa, which is listed at three hundred and forty two thousand. The gap is just two hundred and thirty nine square kilometres. For a country you might know better, try Germany. Drop it onto Rajasthan and it spills over the edges, but only just. Germany is only about four and a half percent bigger. Finland is almost a perfect fit too.

Next come two neighbours that are nearly the same size as each other. Madhya Pradesh, about three hundred and eight thousand square kilometres, matches Oman on the Arabian Peninsula almost exactly. Oman is bigger by only about twelve hundred. Maharashtra is just five hundred and thirty nine square kilometres smaller than Madhya Pradesh, and its twin is Italy. Put the whole boot, Sicily and Sardinia included, onto Maharashtra, and the state still comes out about two percent bigger.

Then Uttar Pradesh, our opening match. The United Kingdom is about fifteen hundred square kilometres bigger, which is a rounding error at this size. But Britain isn't its only twin. Uganda is listed at two hundred and forty one and a half thousand, and Ghana and Romania are both about two hundred and thirty eight and a half thousand. Four countries, all within about one percent of Uttar Pradesh.

Gujarat, about one hundred and ninety six thousand square kilometres, lines up with Senegal on the west coast of Africa. The difference is under five hundred square kilometres. Just behind it is Karnataka, about one hundred and ninety two thousand, and Karnataka's twin is Uruguay in South America, only about sixteen hundred square kilometres bigger. Syria is a close runner up, a little smaller than both.

Andhra Pradesh today, after Telangana was carved out of it, is about one hundred and sixty three thousand square kilometres. That makes it a twin of Tunisia, just six hundred and forty square kilometres apart. Odisha, at about one hundred and fifty six thousand, is the first state on our list that is clearly bigger than its neighbours abroad. It's about five percent larger than Bangladesh, and larger than Nepal as well.

Chhattisgarh, about one hundred and thirty five thousand square kilometres, is a close match for Greece, which comes in about three thousand smaller. And Tamil Nadu, about one hundred and thirty thousand, has one of the tightest twins on this list: Nicaragua in Central America. The two are just three hundred and thirteen square kilometres apart.

Telangana covers about one hundred and twelve thousand square kilometres. Its twin is Honduras, Nicaragua's neighbour, only four hundred and fifteen apart. Bulgaria and Cuba are both a little smaller. Bihar, about ninety four thousand, matches Hungary in central Europe to within about eleven hundred square kilometres. Portugal is close behind.

Now one of the closest pairs of all. West Bengal covers eighty eight thousand seven hundred and fifty two square kilometres. Jordan covers eighty eight thousand seven hundred and ninety four. That's a difference of forty two square kilometres, a rounding error for a state that size. And at the other end of the Himalaya, Arunachal Pradesh is the twin of Austria, another mountain country, just one hundred and forty one square kilometres apart.

Jharkhand, about eighty thousand square kilometres, pairs with Czechia in the middle of Europe, about eight hundred and fifty apart. Assam, on the Brahmaputra, pairs with Serbia. And by coincidence, that gap is also about eight hundred and fifty square kilometres.

Into the hills. Himachal Pradesh, about fifty six thousand square kilometres, matches Croatia, the long, curved country on the Adriatic. Uttarakhand, about fifty three thousand, is roughly four percent bigger than Bosnia and Herzegovina. And Punjab, about fifty thousand, is the twin of Costa Rica, a country famous for its rainforests and wildlife, less than eight hundred square kilometres apart.

Haryana, about forty four thousand square kilometres, sits between two European countries: a little bigger than Denmark, and a little smaller than Estonia. Then comes Kerala, about thirty nine thousand. Its twin is right next door to India: Bhutan, only four hundred and fifty eight square kilometres smaller. Kerala is also bigger than the whole of the Netherlands.

The Northeast is full of small but surprisingly close matches. Meghalaya and Manipur are each about twenty two thousand square kilometres, and both are twins of Israel. Mizoram is a little bigger than Slovenia. Nagaland is a little smaller than Kuwait. And then there's Tripura: ten thousand four hundred and eighty six square kilometres. Lebanon: ten thousand four hundred and fifty two. A gap of just thirty four square kilometres. That's the closest twin of all twenty eight states.

Last, the two smallest states. Sikkim, about seven thousand square kilometres, falls between two island nations, bigger than Brunei and smaller than the island of Cyprus. And Goa, India's smallest state at about three thousand seven hundred square kilometres, is still about one point four times the size of Luxembourg. So even India's smallest state is bigger than a country in Europe.

Here's the scoreboard of the closest twins. In sixth place, Tamil Nadu and Nicaragua, three hundred and thirteen square kilometres apart. Fifth, Manipur and Israel. Fourth, Rajasthan and the Republic of the Congo. Third, Arunachal Pradesh and Austria. Second, West Bengal and Jordan, forty two apart. And the winner, Tripura and Lebanon, just thirty four square kilometres apart.

Why does this matter? Because on a map of the world, India's states look like small pieces of one big country. In reality, Indian states are the size of European nations, African nations and Central American nations. Rajasthan alone covers nearly as much land as Germany. Area is only half of the story, though. Uttar Pradesh and Britain are the same size, but how many people live in each is a very different question, and a story for another video.
So, which twin surprised you most? Tell me your state and its country twin in the comments. And if you'd like to see the population version next, subscribe to True Scale.
